email.body1:
Mike, saw Stampli landed G2's Leader Quadrant for AP automation and the top customer satisfaction spot in a field of 73.

That kind of category momentum usually means more in-market finance teams surfacing than the org can act on before the signal goes cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Stampli off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Mike, quick follow-up for Stampli.

From a RevOps seat, the leak is rarely the signals, it's the latency between a signal firing and a rep actually touching the account, and that lag is exactly where measurable pipeline quietly disappears before anyone catches it.

Worth 15 minutes? I'll walk you through a teardown of your current outbound and three specific things I'd change. Our best practices alone usually lift response rates 50 to 70 percent.
email.body3:
Mike, last bit of proof for Stampli.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Stampli's reply rate likely compares to other B2B software companies. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Mike, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If tightening signal-to-action latency isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Owning RevOps through a growth stretch is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your RevOps motion? I'll tailor it to Stampli either way.
